doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Advice to students: learn the basics and get out in the world
summary: Heard says to learn the basics, then get out and make people smile and dance, rather than rely on schooling.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Have you got any more questions, Mike?

I just would like to ask you if you wanted to leave a word with students that you knew would be watching this interview, things that you could tell them about music, to put the magic in it, what would you tell them?

Well clinics don’t like to hire me because what I have to say I say in about 15-20 seconds. You learn the basics and you get out in the world. You know you learn what the music’s about, and that’s it. It ain’t about schoolwork, you know it ain’t about nothing like that, you know. And if you want it bad enough you’ll get it. Everybody doesn’t accomplish those ends, you know what I mean? But if that’s what you want to do, that’s what you do. Some guys go to institutes of higher learning and they, like your Juilliards and all that stuff, and you have other guys who went there for like a month and dropped out and became legends like Miles and you know, other people, you know? So it all depends on the artist, you know? But you learn the basics and then get out of the way, you make somebody smile or tap their foot, and get up and dance. That’s it. There’s nothing else. Oh yeah, and you’ve got to put some of the creator in there. That’s where it’s all coming from. That’s the part about getting out of the way.
